Assert that a stock and its flows add up over periods

Source: R/reconcile.R
ensure_stock_flow.Rd

A checkpoint for an account over periods: the population at the end of a year must be the population at the end of the year before, plus the born and the immigrated, minus the dead and the emigrated. For a population statistic it is the check that catches most, since every person who is lost or counted twice between the stock and the flows breaks it. Returns data, so it can sit in the middle of a pipeline.

Usage

ensure_stock_flow(
  data,
  time,
  stock,
  inflow,
  outflow,
  by = NULL,
  stock_at = c("end", "start"),
  tolerance = 0,
  success_msg = NULL,
  warn_msg = NULL,
  abort_msg = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, a database table (dbplyr, e.g. DuckDB) or an Arrow table or dataset; see Database and Arrow tables.

time

The period column (one column).

stock

The stock column (one column).

inflow, outflow

Columns of flows into and out of the stock (tidy-select, one or more each), e.g. c(born, immigrated).

by

Columns grouping the account (tidy-select), e.g. sex, or NULL (default) for one account.

stock_at

"end" (default) or "start": when in the period the stock is counted.

tolerance

The largest difference that is accepted. Default 0.

success_msg

Message shown when the rule holds. If NULL (default), it is "Check passed: <message>" when warn_msg or abort_msg is given, so the console names every check that ran, and a description of the check otherwise.

warn_msg

Message shown when the account does not add up and no abort_msg is set. Defaults to a description of the check.

abort_msg

If provided, cli::cli_abort() is called with this message when the rule is broken. If NULL (default), a warning is issued instead.

Value

data invisibly, unchanged.

Details

data holds one row per period (and per group, with by): the stock and the flows during the period, as counted from the registers. Inflows and outflows may be several columns each; they are added up per row.

With stock_at = "end" (default) the stock is counted at the end of each period, so it is the stock before plus the period's flows. With stock_at = "start" it is counted at the start, so it is the stock before plus the flows of the period before.

On failure the periods where the account does not add up are reported, with expected (the stock before plus the flows) and difference (the stock minus expected). The first period of each group has no stock before it and is not checked. A period missing in the middle makes the next one compared with the one before the gap; find such gaps with ensure_balanced(). Rows with a missing stock or flow are not checked.

The table is small, one row per period and group, so a database or Arrow table is fetched into R before the check.

See also

ensure_reconciled() to compare microdata with a published table, checkpoints.

Examples

account <- data.frame(
  year       = 2021:2024,
  population = c(56000, 56100, 56210, 56300),
  born       = c(800, 820, 790, 810),
  immigrated = c(2000, 2100, 2050, 2200),
  dead       = c(500, 520, 510, 530),
  emigrated  = c(2200, 2300, 2280, 2330)
)
# 2023 has 60 persons more than its flows give, so 2024 has 60 fewer
ensure_stock_flow(account, year, population,
                  inflow = c(born, immigrated), outflow = c(dead, emigrated))
#> Warning: The account does not add up: population by year
#> ℹ 2 rows
#>   Difference: total 0, largest 60
#> ℹ The rows:
#>      year population difference expected  born immigrated  dead emigrated
#>     <int>      <dbl>      <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl>      <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#>   1  2023      56210         60    56150   790       2050   510      2280
#>   2  2024      56300        -60    56360   810       2200   530      2330
